features.name: ack_then_counterexample_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the OP's argument and then, in that same comment, present a counter-example?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Read argument only to identify which OP claims/components a comment refers to. Return 1 if at least one single comment (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific component, claim or premise of the OP's argument is valid/correct/fair (not mere generic politeness or vague agreement) in its own assertions, and (b) afterwards in that same comment presents a counter-example (a specific case, instance or scenario that contradicts or challenges the OP's view). Both conditions must be met within one comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Acknowledgment must be by the commenter, not merely quoted OP text. Ignore any text where the OP announces a view change, awards a delta, or reports the outcome, and post-outcome resolution updates; generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

h0: ack_then_counterexample_comment has no association with delta (view change) rate.
h1: Discussions with ack_then_counterexample_comment = 1 have a higher view change rate than those with 0.
note: Assumes "discussions where counter-arguments..." means at least one comment satisfies the conjunction (any-comment). Association only. OC_comments order carries no chronology; "before" is interpreted within a single comment's text. Comments may contain outcome announcements or delta-related text, which the prompt excludes as evidence. The argument column is used only to identify the OP's components; current text may include edits.
